name: Cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish; not canned)
scope_note: Cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish), fresh or frozen, not canned. Lead binds EU cephalopods 300; cadmium binds EU cephalopods 1000; inorganic arsenic binds the EU cephalopods 50; total mercury binds the EU lower-mercury 300. MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds India all-fishery 12000 (the only on-scope sovereign for molluscan cephalopods); Ni/Al screened; Sn/Cr-VI not-material. Canned cephalopods route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

Pb.basis: edible portion, wet weight. EU 2023/915 cephalopods Pb 300 (Israel octopus/squid 300 concurs); the looser CR/PA/PY cephalopod 1000 is not adopted.

Cd.basis: edible portion, wet weight. EU 2023/915 cephalopods Cd 1000 (Costa Rica/Israel concur); the looser TH/PH/GSO/PY cephalopod 2000 is not adopted.

tAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic 1000 (Paraguay cephalopod molluscs; AU-NZ molluscs).

iAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic. EU Reg. 2025/1891 cephalopods iAs 50 (the strictest species-specific inorganic-arsenic seafood line).

tHg.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Cephalopods are within the EU 2023/915 lower-mercury 'cephalopods/marine gastropods' listing (0.3 mg/kg = 300).

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling (300) is stricter than the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML reaching cephalopods (general fishery MeHg 500), so passing tHg guarantees MeHg compliance; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg lower-mercury ceiling (EU 2023/915, 300); no sovereign MeHg ML sits below it
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU; US-FDA; MX; TH; PH; HK

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for cephalopods (EU 2024/1987 nickel is plant-food/seaweed only). Screened rather than assigned a mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign cephalopod Ni ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: Fresh/frozen cephalopods have no tinplate contact; tin is a can-migration analyte and no sovereign sets a non-canned cephalopod tin matrix limit (audit-affirmed). If canned, certified under the canned-seafood subcategory.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to canned-seafood Sn if tinplate-packed.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No non-canned cephalopod Sn ML; canned-seafood Sn limits are can-only
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: Codex CXS 193; EU; US-FDA; MX; CR; HK

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seafood; aluminium in cephalopods is background, managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total chromium. India FSSAI 2016 all-fishery-products total-Cr 12000 is the only on-scope sovereign total-chromium limit reaching cephalopods (HK Cap 132V regulates fish/crustaceans/oysters, not cephalopods, so its 1000 is not directly on-scope here).

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (India all-fishery 12000); no Cr-VI food ML exists and Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) in a reducing animal-tissue matrix. Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in cephalopods.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (India all-fishery 12000)
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; India; HK; EPA (water only)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)
